evals.prompt: It's Monday. I've got 38 accounts and about 8 hours this week for proactive work. Who should I reach out to and what do I send them?
evals.expected_output: A ranked outreach queue built from a sweep of all seven signal families, with suppression gates applied and printed, ranked by Outreach Priority with arithmetic shown, cut to a stated capacity, plus Outreach Cards with drafted messages below a customer-facing separator, and a Coverage Ledger with a confidence cap.
assertions: Sweeps all seven signal families and reports families with no fired triggers as 'checked, no triggers' rather than omitting them
Asks its clarifying questions as one batched tappable AskUserQuestion ask (scope, capacity, drafts, data as-of) with a recommended option first, rather than one question at a time or as open prose
Does not ask for anything .agents/cs-context.md already answers (segments, notice period, source inventory, book size)
Converts the 8-hour budget into a touch count using stated per-touch minute costs, and states the cut line as a rank
Ranks by Outreach Priority = (ARR / 1000) x Strength x Recency x Timing and shows the arithmetic for at least the top accounts
Uses opt_out_deadline (renewal_date minus notice_period_days) for the Timing multiplier, not the renewal date alone
Prints a Suppressed table naming the gate hit for each suppressed trigger rather than silently dropping it

Every drafted message sits inside a fenced ```text copy block below the CUSTOMER-FACING divider, contains no unfilled [placeholders], and carries no health score, risk band, ARR-at-risk, forecast or save-play language
Ends with a Coverage Ledger over the seven families, a coverage percentage, and a confidence cap
Ends with an Assumptions table (# / Assumption / Why it was needed / If wrong) naming every default it ran on, each with a concrete consequence rather than 'may affect results'

Prints a Register value (Standard or Regulated) on every queued row, computed from the trigger — detractor, escalation or Sev-1, broken integration, failed payment, overdue commitment, price increase, or a churn-risk band of At Risk or worse — rather than chosen while writing (C27)

Every drafted ask carries a specific anchor: a date or window, a named event, a named team or a named artifact. No question in the form 'how is X going', 'how are things', 'are you happy with', 'any feedback on' or 'thoughts on' appears in any draft (C1)
Every Plan row carries a verbatim ask and a non-empty Anchor cell; a touch with an empty Anchor is not emitted (C1)

Every Regulated draft opens on the acknowledgement slot before any explanation — the customer's own quoted words where they voiced the problem, what it cost them in their units where we found it first (C4)
Every Regulated draft contains zero exclamation marks, no superlatives or intensifiers, sentences of 20 words or fewer, and at most one apology (C27)

Any customer-voiced Regulated trigger with no verbatim sentence on record appears in the suppressed/held table under gate 'C4 - acknowledgement source' with the source it requires, and no message is written for it

evals.prompt: Acme's usage dropped about 60% over the last six weeks. Write me an email.
evals.expected_output: A single-trigger Outreach Card: the U1 trigger record with evidence and provenance, the recipient chosen by role and altitude, a three-touch cadence with a stop rule, and a customer-facing draft that obeys the craft rules.
assertions: Separates buying-team usage from aggregate usage, or states UNKNOWN if the team split is unavailable
Checks whether one of our own releases caused the drop before implying the customer changed behaviour
Subject line is 1-4 words and lowercase; the first line of the body does not begin with 'I' or 'We'
Body contains at least two account-specific data points, each carrying a provenance tag naming system, field and window
Contains exactly one ask and an honest exit that makes 'no' cheap to send
Does not contain 'just checking in', 'touching base', 'circling back', 'hope you're well', 'drive adoption' or 'monitor closely'
States a stop rule and a decay/timing window for the trigger rather than an open-ended follow-up plan

The email is emitted inside a fenced ```text block formatted for an email client — plain text, blank lines between paragraphs, no markdown headings, no pipe tables, no ** bold — with real values and no [placeholders]
The single ask is anchored to the drop itself — the date the exports fell, the release, or the named team that stopped — and is never 'how is adoption going' or 'any feedback' (C1)
States the register for the card: Standard for a plain usage drop, Regulated if the drop is attributable to our own release or the account is At Risk or worse (C27)

evals.prompt: Our champion at Vertex just left — her email bounced this morning. Vertex renews 14 Feb and it's a $310k account. What do we do?
evals.expected_output: R1 handled as an escalation-override trigger: routed to save-play rather than the ordinary queue, with a 48-hour window, a parallel rung-1 and rung-3 send, and two drafted messages at different altitudes.
assertions: Treats the hard bounce as an inference with a stated rule and names what would falsify it (e.g. an out-of-office or a forwarding address)
Computes and uses the opt-out deadline from the 14 Feb renewal and the notice period, or marks the notice period UNKNOWN and says the deadline cannot be computed
States the 48-hour window and does not place the trigger in an ordinary three-touch email cadence
Produces two messages at different altitudes: a CSM message to the remaining contact and an exec-signed message to the sponsor
Does not re-send to the bounced address and does not speculate about why the champion left
Flags that this trigger is never suppressed by fatigue caps and routes the account to churn-risk or save-play
The ask to the remaining contact is anchored to a named artifact or date — the work Jamie owned, the 14 Feb renewal, the opt-out deadline — not a general 'how are things' enquiry (C1)

evals.prompt: Leadership wants to know if our outreach programme is working. We sent 240 emails last quarter and retention was 94%. Can I say outreach saved those accounts?
evals.expected_output: A direct no, with the selection-bias explanation, the metric set that is honestly reportable now, and a holdout design that would actually answer the question.
assertions: States plainly that retention cannot be attributed to outreach from observational data, and explains the selection-bias mechanism
Distinguishes activity metrics (reply rate, meeting-booked rate, action rate, time-to-first-touch) from outcome claims
Specifies a randomised holdout: one trigger at a time, account-level randomisation, 10-20% held out, held for a full renewal cycle, outcome pre-registered
Names which triggers must be excluded from any holdout because withholding them would harm the customer (operational triggers such as a broken integration or a failed payment)
Does not produce a dollar figure of 'ARR saved' or any claim of guaranteed or 100% accurate attribution
Recommends measuring reply and meeting-booked rates by trigger ID to set an internal baseline rather than quoting published cold-email benchmarks as targets

Names no customer-success-platform vendor as a source, a recommendation or an example, and quotes no action-rate or leadership-transition-churn benchmark that would require one — such a number is dropped with its source, never kept without it

evals.prompt: I've got a Salesforce export (CSV, three junk rows above the header, ARR column is text with dollar signs) and a usage extract from our warehouse as XLSX. No renewal dates in either. Build me this week's outreach list.
evals.expected_output: An ingest-first run: ingest.py normalises both files, low-confidence column mappings are confirmed before use, the missing renewal dates are marked UNKNOWN and the Timing multiplier is dropped rather than guessed, and a partial queue is produced with a coverage figure, a confidence cap and an Assumptions table.
assertions: Runs ../cs-context/scripts/ingest.py on both files before reading any number, rather than parsing them ad hoc
Reports the per-column mapping confidence and explicitly confirms every mapping below 0.80 with the user before using those columns
Reports the cross-file join rate between the CRM export and the usage extract, and states how many accounts failed to resolve
Produces a partial queue rather than refusing: ranks on (ARR / 1000) x Strength x Recency with the Timing multiplier dropped, and says so
Marks the absent renewal and notice-period fields as 'UNKNOWN — requires ...' and never substitutes a default renewal date or an industry benchmark
Asks for the as-of date of both exports and prints it in the artifact header
Caps queue confidence based on the coverage figure and records every default used in the Assumptions table

evals.prompt: We got an NPS 2 from Priya Raman at Meridian this morning. Her comment was: 'we're doing month-end twice because the sync keeps dropping, and nobody has told us anything for three weeks'. She's their ops lead. $180k account. Write the reply.
evals.expected_output: A single-trigger Outreach Card for V1 with Register: Regulated, a Customer words evidence row carrying Priya's verbatim sentence, a 24-hour window, phone recommended where a number exists, and a draft whose first sentence is her own words, in the regulated register, with one anchored ask.
assertions: Marks the card Register: Regulated, computed from the V1 detractor trigger rather than chosen, and labels the trigger customer-voiced
Carries Priya's sentence as a 'Customer words' row in the Evidence table with speaker, source and date, tiered Observed
The first sentence of the customer-facing draft quotes her own words verbatim, before any explanation, context, our activity or an apology (C4)
Does not open with what we have been doing about the sync, when we noticed it, or the root cause
The draft contains zero exclamation marks and none of: amazing, incredibly, thrilled, delighted, absolutely, hugely, extremely, fantastic (C27)
Every sentence in the draft body is 20 words or fewer, ending in a full stop (C27)
The draft apologises at most once (R20 / C28)
The single ask carries a specific anchor — the duplicated month-end runs, the three weeks of silence, or the sync itself — and is not 'how are things going' or 'any feedback' (C1)
Acts inside the 24-hour V1 window and recommends phone first where a number exists, with the written note as the follow-up
Carries no health score, risk band, ARR-at-risk, forecast or save-play language into the customer-facing text, and the draft sits in a fenced text block below the divider with no placeholders
Makes no commercial ask in the message (R11)

evals.prompt: Meridian scored us 2 on the NPS survey. Just the score, no comment. $180k, ops team of about 20. Draft the outreach.
evals.expected_output: A refusal to write the message: a customer-voiced Regulated trigger with no verbatim on record is held under gate 'C4 - acknowledgement source', with the specific source that would unblock it and a phone call as the recommended action.
assertions: Does not produce a customer-facing email: the V1 trigger is customer-voiced, no verbatim sentence exists on record, and the message is held rather than written (C4)
Names the gate explicitly as 'C4 - acknowledgement source' in the suppressed/held table
Prints 'UNKNOWN - requires ...' naming the specific sources that would supply the acknowledgement: the survey free-text field, a ticket, or a call transcript
Recommends retrieving the quote or phoning the respondent so they say it in their own words, rather than paraphrasing what they probably meant
Invents no complaint, infers no cause, and does not substitute an account-level summary for the customer's own words
Any artifact produced is an internal call plan with an owner and a date, not a customer-facing copy block
The call plan's opening question is anchored — the survey response date, the month-end window, or the named team — not 'how are things going' (C1)
Still applies the 24-hour V1 window to the phone attempt
